parts:
On Thursday, February 4, 2016 at 12:24:36 AM UTC-5, Luke wrote:
That might be the issue. I'm not using the coef() function, I'm extracting the samples of the variables and combining the values myself.

I would use coef(). If you are looking at b[(Intercept) group:?] and b[x group:?] those represent the deviation of group ? from the common intercept or slope respectively. The stan_[g]lmer() functions in rstanarm use the same parameterization that is used in the [g]lmer() functions in lme4, which is described in section 1.1 of a recent article by the lme4 authors

http://www.jstatsoft.org/article/view/v067i01

Ben

parts:
There still seems to be a problem. I've created a cut-and-paste script in R to reproduce the problem, excuse it's crudity, it's the first script in R I've written.
The model from y ~ x + (1|grp) works fine, but the model y ~ x + (x|grp) shows a problem visible by the histogram of posterior marginals and from the result of the coef() function.
Running the model y ~ x + (x|grp) with lme4's lmer function and sending the result to coef() shows a correct fit.

library(rstanarm)
library(ggplot2)
library(lme4)
set.seed(0)
num_grps <- 5
num_pnts_per_grp <- 10
x <- matrix(rnorm(num_pnts_per_grp * num_grps, 1:num_grps, 0.5), nrow=num_grps)
y <- 1:num_grps * 2 + 4 + rep(-1, num_grps) * x + rnorm(x, sd=0.1)
grp <- rep(letters[1:num_grps], num_pnts_per_grp)
df <- data.frame(grp, x=c(x), y=c(y))
p <- ggplot(df, aes(x, y))
p + geom_point(aes(color = grp))

fit <- stan_lmer(y ~ x + (x|grp), data=df, seed=0, chains=8, cores=8, iter=1000)
lmfit <- lmer(y ~ x + (x|grp), data=df)

plot(fit, plotfun="hist", pars=names(fit$stanfit))

coef(fit)
coef(lmfit)

Luke

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: rstanarm: how to specify a varying slope and intercept hierarchical model
parts: On Thu, Feb 4, 2016 at 2:36 PM, Bob Carpenter <ca...@alias-i.com> wrote:

If you do full Bayes on these models and use posterior means or
medians to estimate, you wouldn't expect the same result as lme4
would you?  Or did you guys implement MML in RStanARM?

For lme4-style models we do HMC or either of the VB algorithms, not MML. It's true that we don't expect the same results, but in this case there's definitely something getting mixed up when we're renaming parameters (to give them more informative names than they have in the Stan code) before returning the results to the user. I've verified that it's only happening with a subset of lme4-style models. And for those models the estimates from Stan look good, there are a just a few misnamed parameters from the user's perspective.

Is there a writeup somewhere of the expression language for models
and the algorithms you're using?
Do you mean for the lme4-style language?

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: rstanarm: how to specify a varying slope and intercept hierarchical model
parts:
On Thursday, February 4, 2016 at 2:37:53 PM UTC-5, Bob Carpenter wrote:
If you do full Bayes on these models and use posterior means or
medians to estimate, you wouldn't expect the same result as lme4
would you?
Strictly speaking, no, but the default prior on the group-specific parameters is pretty weak. In this case, we did get something similar but messed up the indices in the output.
Or did you guys implement MML in RStanARM?
No

Is there a writeup somewhere of the expression language for models
and the algorithms you're using?

Not really, we're mostly just relying on foo's syntax in stan_foo. The lme4::glmer and gamm4::gamm4 syntaxes are the only ones that are tricky

http://www.jstatsoft.org/article/view/v067i01

has the syntax for glmer and I myself don't really understand how gamm4 extends the spline stuff onto the lme4 syntax.

The possible algorithms are NUTS (always), meanfield / fullrank ADVI (except for stan_lm where it didn't work well in tests), and LBFGS (except for stan_lm, stan_glmer --- because plain optimization doesn't make sense --- and things that call stan_glmer like stan_lmer, stan_gamm4, stan_glmer.nb, etc.). Those are briefly explained in help("rstanarm-package").

Ben

messages.author: fc5d3270037d7478
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: rstanarm: how to specify a varying slope and intercept hierarchical model
parts:
And just to clarify, because I think I see the confusion now, it's still true that the model was being estimated correctly in the previous version. But the labelling mistake was occurring immediately after estimation when renaming the parameters (changing their names from those used in the underlying Stan code to the more substantive names returned to the user). So it was happening after estimation but before returning the fitted model object. That is, the fitted model object had the right estimates in it, they were just labeled incorrectly. The post-estimation functions were working properly, but they assumed the labels were correct. 

Anyway, I'm glad we got that sorted out. Thanks for your patience!

Jonah

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: rstanarm: how to specify a varying slope and intercept hierarchical model
parts:

And just to clarify, because I think I see the confusion now, it's still true that the model was being estimated correctly in the previous version. But the labelling mistake was occurring immediately after estimation when renaming the parameters (changing their names from those used in the underlying Stan code to the more substantive names returned to the user). So it was happening after estimation but before returning the fitted model object. That is, the fitted model object had the right estimates in it, they were just labeled incorrectly. The post-estimation functions were working properly, but they assumed the labels were correct. 

Anyway, I'm glad we got that sorted out. Thanks for your patience!

And thus everyone needs to install the new version of rstanarm from CRAN and redo any lme4-style model from a previous version of rstanarm (stan_lmer, stan_glmer, stan_glmer.nb, stan_gamm4) that has group-specific coefficients.

Ben
